title: Lunch on the Grass
checkpoint: Year 1 Spring 1, week 1 — Phase 4: words with adjacent consonants, using sounds already taught
note_for_grown_ups: A Phase 4 book with clusters like crisp, plum and sting. Encourage your child to say each sound in the cluster clearly before blending the whole word.

pages.illustration: Fig the caterpillar and Moss the hedgehog laying out a small picnic on a checked cloth in the grass. Cheerful and domestic.

pages.text: They sat on the soft grass.
pages.illustration: The two of them settled on the soft grass from a low viewpoint, grass blades framing the shot like a forest. Green and warm.
Fig holding a single potato crisp bigger than his own head, about to bite the edge. Comic scale, lovely crisp texture.
Moss with a deep purple plum held in both paws, juice already on his chin. Rich colour against his brown spikes.
A wasp cutting across the page in a hard straight line, both picnickers frozen mid-bite watching it go. Tension.
The wasp gone off the edge of the frame, both of them exhaling, Moss's spikes settling back down. Relief and comedy.
Both flat on their backs on the cloth with full tummies, hats over their eyes, deeply asleep. Dappled shade.
Closing page: the empty cloth with crumbs and a plum stone, late afternoon light across the grass, two contented shapes asleep beside it.
